candidates.claim: getSecretPayload does not send an Accept header; the reference says the Accept header must be set to one of the secret's content_types for GET /payload. signal-openstack adds no Accept header, so the call can return 406 (mapped to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) or the wrong content type. Also mapKmError has no mapping for 406/415, which the reference lists for these endpoints.
candidates.evidence: Code: `km.get(`v1/secrets/${encodeURIComponent(input.secretId)}/payload`)` with no options/headers; grep of packages/signal-openstack/src/client.ts shows only a Content-Type default, no Accept. Reference (secrets.rst 'GET /v1/secrets/{uuid}/payload'): 'When making a request for a secret's payload, you must set the accept header to one of the values listed in the ``content_types`` attribute of a secret's metadata.' Status codes: '406 | Not Acceptable'; POST /v1/secrets lists '415 | Unsupported media-type'. mapKmError codeMap covers only 400/401/403/404/409 (lines 43-49).

candidates.claim: updateSecret uses PUT /v1/secrets/{id}, which the reference restricts to metadata-only secrets without a payload; the router offers it for any secret, so editing a secret that already has a payload fails (400/409), surfacing as a generic error. candidates.evidence: Code: `.put(`v1/secrets/${encodeURIComponent(input.secretId)}`, input.payload, { headers: { "Content-Type": input.payload_content_type } })`. Reference (secrets.rst 'PUT /v1/secrets/{uuid}'): 'Add the payload to an existing metadata-only secret, such as one made by sending a POST /v1/secrets request that does not include the ``payload`` attribute.' and note 'This action can only be done for a secret that doesn't have a payload.' Headers table lists optional 'Content-Encoding'. Documented status codes: 204, 401, 404 only.

candidates.evidence: Code: `limit: z.number().default(20)`. Reference (secrets.rst/containers.rst/orders.rst): 'limit | integer | The maximum number of records to return (up to 100). The default limit is 10.' Pagination: code sends offset/limit (consistent with the documented offset/limit), UI page size 50 (OrdersList.tsx:17); `next`/`previous` are parsed in the schema but unused.

candidates.claim: The Reveal Payload button (and the detail views generally) is not gated by the `key-manager:secrets:payload` permission, which is mapped server-side but never read by any client code. A user without payload rights still sees the button and the server procedure fetches the plaintext secret; only Barbican's own ACLs stop it.
candidates.evidence: git grep of usePermissions/permissions[ under key-manager/ (at head) shows usage only in ContainersList, OrdersList and SecretsList (list/create/delete); SecretDetailsView, ContainerDetailsView and OrderDetailsView have none. `key-manager:secrets:payload` appears only in usePermissions.ts type and permissionRouter mappings.

candidates.claim: None of the KeyManager mutations or the payload query enforce a server-side canUser/policy check; they rely only on projectScopedProcedure and Barbican's own authorization. The policy file key-manager.json (viewer/editor split) is therefore advisory UI-hiding only, including for getSecretPayload (plaintext key material) and delete/create/update.
candidates.evidence: All procedures in keyManagerRouter.ts go straight from projectScopedProcedure to km.get/post/put/del with no call to the policy engine; permissionRouter.ts only exposes the canUser query.
candidates.precedent: Network routers (e.g. floatingIpRouter) also do not call the policy engine in mutations, so this matches existing convention, but the review rubric requires server enforcement.

candidates.claim: Decrypted secret payload is fetched via a TanStack Query useQuery (enabled:false + refetch) and so stays in the client query cache after 'Hide' (default gcTime 5 min, also refetchable/shared across components), and is returned as `res.text()` which corrupts binary payloads. Plaintext secrets remaining in cache longer than needed is a data-protection concern; consider a mutation or gcTime:0 and clear on hide/unmount.
candidates.evidence: setShowPayload(false) on Hide only toggles UI state; no cache removal or gcTime option on the query.

candidates.claim: ID/ref inputs interpolated into outbound Barbican paths are unvalidated `z.string()`; encodeURIComponent does not encode `.`, so `secretId`/`containerId`/`orderId`/`secretName` of `..` yields `v1/secrets/..` style paths that a URL normaliser collapses (e.g. DELETE v1/containers/.. -> v1/). Also secret_ref/secret_refs entries are arbitrary strings forwarded to Barbican, and `sort` is free text split into sort_key/sort_dir. Low impact (same project token, same service) but should be constrained with uuid()/regex.
candidates.evidence: `const resourceIdInput = z.object({ secretId: z.string() })`, containerIdInput/orderIdInput the same; deleteContainerSecret uses `secretName: z.string()` in the path; addContainerSecret `secret_ref: z.string()`; pagination `offset`/`limit` are unbounded z.number() (no int/min/max).

candidates.claim: mapKmError attaches the raw upstream error as `cause` for every failure; if the tRPC error formatter or logger serialises causes this can expose OpenStack internals, and the secret payload in createSecret/updateSecret bodies could flow into logged errors. Worth confirming the error formatter strips `cause`.
candidates.evidence: `return new TRPCError({ code: ..., message: ..., cause: error })`
